subject: Post-demo SLO qualification: throughput/latency sizing and GPU variants
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Parker <alex.parker@altiushealth.com>, Sabrina Holt <sabrina.holt@altiushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap and action items: SLO targets, sizing, and GPU variants

Hi Alex / Sabrina —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Short recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up a pilot slab:

What we heard from your side:
- Primary latency SLO: 95th percentile (p95) end-to-end generation for single-turn chat at <= 150ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens).
- Streaming requirement: token-by-token streaming for longer responses (up to 1024 tokens) with first-byte <= 80ms and steady-state token rate of ~40–50 tokens/sec for the model family you prefer.
- Peak concurrency: 200 concurrent sessions during business hours; average concurrent 45.
- Throughput floor for reserved capacity: sustained 600 requests/min (~10 RPS) with burst to 60 RPS for 5–10 minutes.

Our suggested sizing options (to validate in pilot):
- H100 80GB slab (quantized int8) — best latency and headroom for concurrency; good for streaming and KV-cache heavy workloads, higher $/hour.
- A100 80GB (bf16 / q4) — balanced option; slightly higher p95 for streaming start but lower cost than H100 in our price bands.
- L40S (q4_0) — cost-efficient for inferencing lower-compute variants, expected higher p95 on first-byte for long form streaming but good token/sec when batchable.

Pilot scope we propose:
1) 48-hour microbenchmark on each GPU variant with your representative prompt set (we'll run both short-turn chat and long-stream tests).
2) Collect p50/p95/p99 for first-byte + tail for streaming and non-streaming paths, tokens/sec, KV cache hit/miss effect, and cost per 1k tokens.
3) Verify reserved throughput mapping (how many virtual RPS/slab) and validate autoscale guardrails for 60 RPS bursts.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Confirm the p95 target above (150ms) or update.
- Share representative prompt set and a short eval corpus (50–100 examples) we can use in the bench.
- Give procurement window / any firewall/VPC setup requirements.

Attachments: call recording + initial SLO matrix (attached).

I'll loop in engineering (Marissa + Ben) to capture technical acceptance criteria and timeline. If all looks good we can schedule the 48-hour pilot the week of Sep 10.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alex Parker <alex.parker@altiushealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap and action items: SLO targets, sizing, and GPU variants

Thanks Naom — quick technical clarifications / notes for the bench before we lock the pilot:

1) p95 target: 150ms end-to-end for the short prompts is aggressive but achievable on H100 with the model variant we demo'd (7B dense -> int8). A100 is likely to land around 160–220ms depending on KV cache warm state and batching profile. L40S we should expect 220–400ms in cold-starts.

2) Streaming first-byte goal: 80ms first-byte requires low batching and small queueing windows. We'll configure continuous batching with a max batching delay of 4ms for this pilot to optimize first-byte. If you have a strict first-byte SLA we should prioritize H100.

3) Concurrency mapping: based on model and sequence length assumptions (avg prompt 60 tokens, avg response 120 tokens) —
   - H100 slab (48 GPUs logical): ~250 concurrent sessions under our default runtime config with p95 headroom;
   - A100 slab: ~160 concurrent sessions;
   - L40S / mixed: ~120 concurrent sessions.

4) Throughput -> reserved slab equivalence: we'll provide a small calculator in the pilot report showing how many reserved slabs you should commit to for steady 10 RPS and for 60 RPS bursts. This will include cost-per-token delta for int8 quantized vs bf16.

5) Fall-back policy: recommend pre-configured fallback to a cheaper A100 variant for non-streamed bursts to avoid overprovisioning H100 for batchable workloads. We'll include routing policies in the pilot config.

I'll attach a quick bench config (pilot-slo-matrix.xlsx) with workloads, expected metrics, and estimated run time. Planning to provision baseline infra tomorrow morning so we can start the bench Monday if you share the prompt set by end of day Friday.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Parker <alex.parker@altiushealth.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap and action items: SLO targets, sizing, and GPU variants

Hi Naomi / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear notes. A few quick confirmations from us:
- The p95 150ms target is our goal for short-turn UI responses. If we see H100 meets it in the bench we'll prioritize that path; otherwise we're open to an H100+A100 hybrid for cost/latency balance.
- We'll share the prompt set and 75 eval examples by EOD Friday.
- Procurement: we can sign a short-term reserved pilot SLA for 30 days; legal asks a doc listing fallback behavior and data retention for the pilot (SOC/retention note). Sabrina will send the procurement timeline.
- One ask: can the bench surface first-byte times per region? We have users in both us-west and us-east — we'd like region-level latencies.

If you can include region splits in the bench and the fallback routing policy skeleton, we are good to kick off. Schedule-wise Sep 11 start works on our side.

Thanks,

Perfect — thanks Alex. Quick summary of agreed next steps and owners: 

1) Altius -> send prompt set + 75 eval examples (Alex) — due EOD Fri Aug 31.
2) Marissa -> provision pilot slabs (H100 / A100 / L40S variants), configure continuous batching delay = 4ms, enable region split (us-west / us-east) in bench. Target: provision by Mon Sep 10.
3) Ben -> prepare fallback routing policy draft and short appendix for pilot SLA covering data retention and SOC-related pilot notes. Due Sep 5.
4) Naomi -> finalize commercial pilot terms (30 day reserved pilot) and get procurement contact from Sabrina to expedite.

We will attach the bench results + slab calculator and a recommendation doc at the end of the 48-hour runs. If anything changes ping me on Slack (naomi_f) — I'll schedule a 30-min sync on Sep 12 to review results.

Thanks all — looking forward to moving this into a short pilot.
